text:
jamal: Heads up — after the v1.38 merge we're seeing a clear perf regression on the serving runtime. p95 up ~2x, p99 spikes and CPU utilization on the kernel workers jumps. Repro on CI perf job and locally with sampled traffic. Can someone start a bisect and check kernel selector + kv cache interaction? :eyes:

ci-bot: perf-regression detected on branch release/v1.38 (job: perf/stable-snapshot). Baseline p99=2.0s -> current p99=4.8s. Suspected range: commits 7a1f3b..d4c2e9.

maria: copying bisect steps — start by running the perf harness with the same seed and perf config, then narrow by half. Quick commands:```bash
git checkout release/v1.38
git bisect start
git bisect bad d4c2e9
git bisect good 7a1f3b
# run perf script, mark good/bad
```

nate: I ran a fast bisect on a sampled cluster and it pointed at commit d9e7b2a — that one changes the kernel selector heuristics (prefer simd path for <=64 tokens). Also touched KV cache prefetch timing. I think the selector change causes more frequent kernel switches which invalidates some cache assumptions.

alex: I can run a more controlled profile. Running the perf harness now with kv cache warm vs cold and delta sampling. Command I used:```bash
./perf/run.sh --workload=chat --tokens=64 --iters=250 --profile --kv-warm=true
```

jamal: thanks. nate — do you have the exact commit id we should revert/cherry-pick? If it's the selector tweak we might want a short revert on release branch and then re-introduce after tests.

nate: commit is d9e7b2a (author: @mike). It has this change in selector.c:```c
- if (seq_len <= 64) return simd_kernel;
+ if (seq_len <= 64 && est_cache_hits > 2) return simd_kernel;
```
that `est_cache_hits` logic seems off for bursty chat where kv cache warms asynchronously. The perf flamegraphs show extra dispatch overhead.

ci-bot: perf job details: https://ci.internal/perf/1845126789 — p99 breakdown: kernel-select 0.4s -> 1.9s, dispatch overhead + queues 0.3s -> 1.3s.

maria: proposal: quick cherry-pick revert (revert d9e7b2a) to release/v1.38, run the perf job, if green ship hotfix. Steps:```bash
# on release branch
git checkout release/v1.38
git pull origin release/v1.38
# create quick branch
git checkout -b hotfix/revert-selector-d9e7b2a
# cherry-pick revert commit
git revert --no-edit d9e7b2a
# push and open PR to release with perf CI enabled
git push origin hotfix/revert-selector-d9e7b2a
```

alex: I'm 10m from finishing a perf run. If the revert fixes p99 I'll run a longer smoke test with kvcache toggled.

release-manager: please add an explicit test in the PR that runs the perf harness on the release runner and includes kvcache warm/cold scenarios. We need the CI artifact link in the PR description. Also include the original commit SHA in the PR body and sign-off from eng-runtime.

nate: quick local flamegraph snippet (hot path):```text
flamegraph: kernel_select -> dispatch -> kernel_run_loop -> memcpy
% time: kernel_select 38% (was 9% before d9e7b2a)
```

jamal: alex — any early results?

alex: early numbers look promising after revert: p95 ~ back to baseline, p99 down to 2.1s in the quick run. I'll kick off the CI perf job on the branch now. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: perf/stable-snapshot job queued for hotfix/revert-selector-d9e7b2a (run id 1845127002).

maria: also please verify with a replay of real traffic from the golden set (we saw this only on chat-like workloads). Use `./tools/replay --trace=golden-chat --kv-warm=true`.

alex: replay done, looks good: p99 ~2.0s, memory and cpu stable. Pushed results to the PR as artifacts.

release-manager: good — once CI passes and ENG sign-off we can cut a patch release. @jamal please add the cherry-pick PR link and a short note for release notes about reverting selector tweak due to kv cache regression.

jamal: PR created: https://git.internal/r/repo/pull/7623 (cherry-pick revert d9e7b2a). CI perf job passed on the release runner. Requesting eng-runtime review and sign-off.

nate: reviewed and approved. We'll schedule a follow-up to rework selector heuristics and add more tests for kvcache interplay.

jamal: plan: ship hotfix; follow-up ticket to add unit + perf tests before re-landing. Thanks everyone. :shipit:
